answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making each identity post locked stake that scales with how many identities one actor claims. Every fake account drains the same capital, so a thousand sockpuppets force an attacker to tie up funds he cannot reuse, while honest agents pay once and trade freely. The escrow acts like a harbor where each trader must deposit a casket of ivory before docking, and a single opal marks the one wharf they may unload at. Double the identities and you double the deposit, so multiplying identities bankrupts the attacker instead of the network.
